item.name: structured data
item.description: A standardized format for providing information about a page and classifying its content.
item.grounding_span: Structured data is a standardized format for providing information about a page and classifying the page content.

item.name: dataset discovery
item.description: Google's approach to making datasets findable via schema.org and other metadata standards.
item.grounding_span: our approach to dataset discovery

item.name: Dataset
item.description: The schema.org type describing a dataset and its metadata; the primary asset class of this document.
item.grounding_span: The full definition of `Dataset` is available at [schema.org/Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset).

item.name: DataCatalog
item.description: A repository catalog to which a dataset belongs.
item.grounding_span: The full definition of `DataCatalog` is available at [schema.org/DataCatalog](https://schema.org/DataCatalog).

item.name: DataDownload
item.description: A downloadable distribution of a dataset in a given format at a content URL.
item.grounding_span: The full definition of `DataDownload` is available at [schema.org/DataDownload](https://schema.org/DataDownload).

item.name: metadata standards
item.description: Standards for describing a dataset (what it is about, who created it, etc.) added to pages that describe datasets.
item.grounding_span: other metadata standards that can be added to pages that describe datasets.

item.name: rich result
item.description: An enhanced search result display eligible content can qualify for.
item.grounding_span: You must include the required properties for your content to be eligible for display as a rich result.

item.name: canonical (landing) page
item.description: The authoritative page for a dataset, distinct from listing pages that reference many datasets.
item.grounding_span: the canonical ("landing") pages for each dataset

item.name: source and provenance
item.description: Representation of situations where a dataset is a copy of, based upon, or aggregated from other datasets.
item.grounding_span: It is common for open datasets to be republished, aggregated, and to be based on other datasets.
item.location: Guidelines > Source and provenance best practices

item.name: identifier
item.description: An identifier such as a DOI or Compact Identifier attached to a dataset.
item.grounding_span: An identifier, such as a DOI or a Compact Identifier.

item.name: license
item.description: A license under which the dataset is distributed.
item.grounding_span: A license under which the dataset is distributed.

item.name: crawling and indexing
item.description: The process by which Google finds, crawls, and indexes pages; changes take time to reflect.
item.grounding_span: Allow time for re-crawling and re-indexing.

item.name: tabular dataset
item.description: A dataset organized primarily as a grid of rows and columns.
item.grounding_span: A [tabular dataset](https://www.w3.org/TR/tabular-data-model/#intro) is one organized primarily in terms of a grid of rows and columns.
item.location: Structured data type definitions > Tabular datasets

item.name: spatial coverage
item.description: The spatial aspect of a dataset expressed as a point, shape, or named location.
item.grounding_span: You can provide a single point that describes the spatial aspect of the dataset.

item.name: temporal coverage
item.description: The time interval the dataset's data covers, expressed in ISO 8601.
item.grounding_span: The data in the dataset covers a specific time interval.

item.name: variable measured
item.description: The variable that a dataset measures, such as temperature or pressure.
item.grounding_span: The variable that this dataset measures.

item.name: measurement technique
item.description: The technique, technology, or methodology used in a dataset.
item.grounding_span: The technique, technology, or methodology used in a dataset, which can correspond to the variable(s) described in `variableMeasured`.

item.name: dataset identity (sameAs)
item.description: A reference web page URL that unambiguously indicates the dataset's identity.
item.grounding_span: The URL of a reference web page that unambiguously indicates the dataset's identity.

item.name: keywords
item.description: Keywords summarizing the dataset.
item.grounding_span: Keywords summarizing the dataset.

item.name: structured data manual action
item.description: A penalty causing structured data on a page to be ignored.
item.grounding_span: If you received a structured data manual action against your page, the structured data on the page will be ignored (although the page can still appear in Google Search results).

item.name: required properties
item.description: Properties that must be included for content to be eligible for a rich result.
item.grounding_span: Add the [required properties](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/dataset#structured-data-type-definitions).

item.name: recommended properties
item.description: Optional properties that add more information and can improve user experience.
item.grounding_span: You can also include the recommended properties to add more information about your content, which could provide a better user experience.

item.name: IndexNow protocol
item.description: A protocol by which website owners notify participating search engines that URLs have been added, updated, or deleted.
item.grounding_span: Search engines adopting the IndexNow protocol agree that submitted URLs will be automatically shared with all other participating search engines.

item.name: URL submission
item.description: Notifying a search engine of changed URLs via an HTTP request to its indexnow endpoint.
item.grounding_span: To submit a set of URLs using an HTTP request issue your POST JSON request to the URL provided by Search Engines.

item.name: Single URL submission
item.description: Submitting one changed URL using an HTTP GET request with url and key parameters.
item.grounding_span: To submit a URL using an HTTP request

item.name: Batch URL submission
item.description: Submitting up to 10,000 URLs at once via an HTTP POST JSON request.
item.grounding_span: You can submit up to 10,000 URLs per post, mixing http and https URLs if needed.

item.name: Verification key
item.description: A hexadecimal key (8–128 chars) that authenticates submissions and proves ownership.
item.grounding_span: Your-key should have a minimum of 8 and a maximum of 128 hexadecimal characters.

item.name: Ownership verification via key
item.description: Proving control of a host by hosting a key file that search engines crawl.
item.grounding_span: To submit URLs, you must "prove" ownership of the host for which URLs are being submitted by hosting at least one text file within the host.

item.name: Key file
item.description: A UTF-8 text file containing the key, hosted on the site so search engines can verify ownership.
item.grounding_span: You must host a UTF-8 encoded text key file {your-key}.txt listing the key in the file at the root directory of your website.

item.name: keyLocation
item.description: A parameter identifying the location of a key file hosted somewhere other than the root directory.
item.grounding_span: specifying the location using the keyLocation variable.

item.name: Host
item.description: The website host that is the unit of ownership and scope for submissions.
item.grounding_span: by hosting at least one text file within the host.

item.name: Search engine
item.description: The machine consumer that receives, verifies, and acts on submitted URLs.
item.grounding_span: the URL provided by the search engine

item.name: Automatic sharing of submitted URLs
item.description: Participating search engines automatically share submitted URLs with each other.
item.grounding_span: submitted URLs will be automatically shared with all other participating search engines

item.name: URI/RFC-3986 conformance
item.description: Submitted URLs must be URL-escaped, encoded, and follow the RFC-3986 URI standard.
item.grounding_span: URL must be URL-escaped and encoded

item.description: Defined HTTP status codes and their meanings for IndexNow submissions.

item.name: Sitemap protocol
item.description: The XML schema and protocol for informing search engines about URLs on a site.
item.grounding_span: This document describes the XML schema for the Sitemap protocol.

item.name: Sitemap
item.description: A file listing the URLs of a site for search engines, consisting of XML tags.
item.grounding_span: The Sitemap protocol format consists of XML tags.

item.name: XML tags
item.description: The tag-based format that a Sitemap is composed of.
item.grounding_span: The Sitemap protocol format consists of XML tags.

item.name: urlset element
item.description: Root element encapsulating the file and referencing the protocol standard via namespace.
item.grounding_span: Specify the namespace (protocol standard) within the `<urlset>` tag.

item.name: url entry
item.description: Parent tag for each URL entry; container of the loc, lastmod, changefreq and priority child tags.
item.grounding_span: Include a entry for each URL, as a parent XML tag.

item.name: loc tag
item.description: Child tag giving the URL of the page.
item.grounding_span: URL of the page. This URL must begin with the protocol (such as http) and end with a trailing slash

item.name: lastmod tag
item.description: Optional tag giving the date of last modification of the page.
item.grounding_span: The date of last modification of the page.

item.name: changefreq tag
item.description: Optional tag hinting how frequently the page is likely to change.
item.grounding_span: How frequently the page is likely to change.

item.name: priority tag
item.description: Optional tag giving the priority of a URL relative to other URLs on the same site.
item.grounding_span: The priority of this URL relative to other URLs on your site.

item.name: entity escaping
item.description: Requirement that all data values in a Sitemap use XML entity escape codes.
item.grounding_span: any data values (including URLs) must use entity escape codes for the characters listed in the table below.

item.name: UTF-8 encoding
item.description: Character encoding required for the Sitemap file.

item.verbatim_text: Data Catalog Vocabulary - United States. The federal metadata standard that data.gov requires for all published datasets. DCAT-US defines which metadata fields are required (such as title, description, modified date, and keywords) and what formats are acceptable for each field. Harvest validation errors occur when dataset metadata does not conform to the DCAT-US schema.
item.grounding_span: Data Catalog Vocabulary - United States. The federal metadata standard that data.gov requires for all published datasets. DCAT-US defines which metadata fields are required (such as title, description, modified date, and keywords) and what formats are acceptable for each field. Harvest validation errors occur when dataset metadata does not conform to the DCAT-US schema.

item.verbatim_text: A DCAT-US metadata field describing how often a dataset is updated. Must use ISO 8601 duration codes in repeating interval format (such as R/P1W for weekly, R/P1M for monthly, R/P1Y for annual) or the literal value 'irregular' for datasets that are no longer updated. Plain English descriptions like 'Weekly' or 'Monthly' are not accepted and cause validation failures.
item.grounding_span: A DCAT-US metadata field describing how often a dataset is updated. Must use ISO 8601 duration codes in repeating interval format (such as R/P1W for weekly, R/P1M for monthly, R/P1Y for annual) or the literal value 'irregular' for datasets that are no longer updated. Plain English descriptions like 'Weekly' or 'Monthly' are not accepted and cause validation failures.

item.verbatim_text: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the email address for the dataset contact. Must be formatted as a single mailto: URI (for example, mailto:contact@agency.gov) with no extra text, no subject lines, no multiple addresses, and no trailing spaces. Common validation failures include appended subject lines, multiple email addresses in one field, or invisible Unicode characters from copy-pasting.
item.grounding_span: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the email address for the dataset contact. Must be formatted as a single mailto: URI (for example, mailto:contact@agency.gov) with no extra text, no subject lines, no multiple addresses, and no trailing spaces. Common validation failures include appended subject lines, multiple email addresses in one field, or invisible Unicode characters from copy-pasting.

item.verbatim_text: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing tags that describe the dataset's subject matter to help users find it in search results. Must be formatted as an array of strings, even if there is only one keyword (for example, ['environment'] not 'environment'). Datasets must have at least one keyword. Both missing keywords and improperly formatted keyword fields cause validation failures.

item.verbatim_text: A DCAT-US metadata field that must contain a URL pointing to the dataset's license document. The field only accepts valid URIs, not plain text descriptions. For most U.S. government public domain datasets, the correct value is https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. Text values like 'Public Domain' or 'None' cause validation failures.

item.verbatim_text: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the date a dataset or its metadata was last updated. Must be formatted in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). The most common harvest error is a malformed modified date where the year and month run together without the required hyphen separator. Missing modified dates also trigger validation failures since this is a required field.

item.verbatim_text: An optional DCAT-US metadata field containing the date a dataset was first published or released. When present, must be formatted in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Like the modified field, issued dates commonly fail validation when the year and month are run together without proper hyphen separators.

item.verbatim_text: The international standard for representing dates and times. ISO 8601 requires dates to be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD with hyphens separating year, month, and day (for example, 2024-03-15). Date format errors are the most common type of harvest validation failure, typically occurring when dates are malformed such as having the year and month run together (201603-01 instead of 2016-03-01).

item.verbatim_text: An international standard for geospatial metadata. Some federal agencies publish their dataset metadata in ISO 19115 or ISO 19115-2 format. When harvesting these sources, the system converts the ISO metadata into DCAT-US format. Transformation errors can occur if the ISO records are missing required elements that are needed for the conversion.

item.verbatim_text: A harvest error that occurs when a metadata field value does not conform to the DCAT-US schema requirements. The harvester can read the record, but a specific field value is formatted incorrectly, contains an unacceptable value, or is missing when required. Validation errors make up approximately 66% of all harvest failures. These errors typically begin with a field name such as '$.modified' or '$.accrualPeriodicity'.

item.verbatim_text: A harvest error that occurs before validation when the harvester cannot read or convert a metadata record at all. These indicate structural problems with the source file itself, such as malformed XML, missing required elements in ISO 19115 records, or unrecognizable record structures. Transformation errors make up approximately 32% of harvest failures and always begin with the phrase 'record failed to transform'.

item.verbatim_text: A dataset is an organized collection of data. The most basic representation of a dataset is data elements presented in tabular form. Each column represents a particular variable. Each row corresponds to a given value of that column’s variable. A dataset may also present information in a variety of non-tabular formats, such as an extensible mark-up language (XML) file, a geospatial data file, or an image file, etc.

item.verbatim_text: A collection of data elements or datasets that make sense to group together. Each community of interest identifies the Data Assets specific to supporting the needs of their respective mission or business functions. Notably, a Data Asset is a deliberately abstract concept. A given Data Asset may represent an entire database consisting of multiple distinct entity classes, or may represent a single entity class.

Each agency typically has one or more harvest sources.

item.name: Linked Data
item.description: A network of standards-based machine-interpretable data across documents and Web sites, followed via embedded links.
item.grounding_span: Linked Data [LINKED-DATA] is a way to create a network of standards-based machine interpretable data across different documents and Web sites.

item.name: JSON-LD
item.description: A lightweight JSON-based syntax to serialize Linked Data.
item.grounding_span: JSON-LD is a lightweight syntax to serialize Linked Data in JSON [RFC8259].

item.name: IRI
item.description: Identifiers fundamental to Linked Data used to identify nodes and properties.
item.grounding_span: IRIs (Internationalized Resource Identifiers [RFC3987]) are fundamental to Linked Data as that is how most nodes and properties are identified.

item.name: context
item.description: A set of rules mapping terms to IRIs for interpreting a JSON-LD document.
item.grounding_span: Simply speaking, a context is used to map terms to IRIs.

item.name: term
item.description: A short word defined in a context that may be expanded to an IRI.
item.grounding_span: A term is a short word defined in a context that may be expanded to an IRI.

item.name: node object
item.description: A map representing zero or more properties of a node in the graph.
item.grounding_span: A node object represents zero or more properties of a node in the graph serialized by the JSON-LD document.

item.name: value object
item.description: A map that has an @value entry, describing a literal node.
item.grounding_span: A value object is a map that has an `@value` entry.

item.name: blank node
item.description: A node that is neither an IRI nor a literal.
item.grounding_span: A node in a graph that is neither an IRI, nor a literal.

item.name: RDF dataset
item.description: A collection of RDF graphs with one default graph and zero or more named graphs.
item.grounding_span: A dataset representing a collection of RDF graphs including exactly one default graph and zero or more named graphs.

item.name: named graph
item.description: A linked data graph identified by an IRI or blank node.
item.grounding_span: A named graph is a linked data graph that is identified by an IRI or blank node.

item.name: default graph
item.description: An unnamed RDF graph of a dataset, which may be empty.
item.grounding_span: The default graph of a dataset is an RDF graph having no name, which may be empty.

item.name: typed value
item.description: A value (a string) together with a type (an IRI).
item.grounding_span: A typed value consists of a value, which is a string, and a type, which is an IRI.

item.name: language-tagged string
item.description: A string with a non-empty BCP47 language tag.
item.grounding_span: A language-tagged string consists of a string and a non-empty language tag as defined by [BCP47].

item.name: base direction
item.description: The direction used when a string has no direction directly associated with it.
item.grounding_span: The base direction is the direction used when a string does not have a direction associated with it directly.

item.name: vocabulary mapping
item.description: A mapping set in the context via @vocab for expanding properties and @type values.
item.grounding_span: The vocabulary mapping is set in the context using the `@vocab` key whose value must be an IRI, a compact IRI, a term, or `null`.

item.name: compact IRI
item.description: An IRI expressed as prefix:suffix without a separate term definition.
item.grounding_span: A compact IRI has the form of prefix:*suffix* and is used as a way of expressing an IRI without needing to define separate term definitions for each IRI contained within a common vocabulary identified by prefix.

item.name: keyword
item.description: A string specific to JSON-LD that is a core part of the language.
item.grounding_span: A string that is specific to JSON-LD

item.name: list
item.description: An ordered sequence of IRIs, blank nodes, and literals.
item.grounding_span: A list is an ordered sequence of IRIs, blank nodes, and literals.

item.name: type coercion
item.description: Context rules that cause a string value to be interpreted as an IRI or typed value.
item.grounding_span: If type coercion rules are specified in the `@context` for a particular term or property IRI, an IRI is generated:

item.name: node identifier
item.description: The @id keyword identifying a node object with an IRI or blank node identifier.

item.name: base IRI
item.description: The IRI used to turn relative IRI references into IRIs.
item.grounding_span: The base IRI is an IRI established in the context, or is based on the JSON-LD document location.

item.name: RDF graph
item.description: A labeled directed graph of nodes connected by directed-arcs.
item.grounding_span: A labeled directed graph, i.e., a set of nodes connected by directed-arcs.

item.name: property
item.description: The name of a directed-arc in a linked data graph.
item.grounding_span: The name of a directed-arc in a linked data graph.

item.name: literal
item.description: An object expressed as a value such as a string or number.
item.grounding_span: An object expressed as a value such as a string or number.

item.name: blank node identifier
item.description: A string identifier for a blank node, beginning with _:.
item.grounding_span: A blank node identifier is a string that can be used as an identifier for a blank node within the scope of a JSON-LD document.

item.name: term definition
item.description: An entry in a context defining a term usable as key, type, or vocabulary item.
item.grounding_span: A term definition is an entry in a context, where the key defines a term which may be used within a map as a key, type, or elsewhere that a string is interpreted as a vocabulary item.

item.name: expanded term definition
item.description: A term definition whose value is a map of keyword keys.
item.grounding_span: An expanded term definition is a term definition where the value is a map containing one or more keyword keys to define the associated IRI, if this is a reverse property, the type associated with string values, and a container mapping.

item.name: JSON-LD document
item.description: A serialization of an RDF dataset.
item.grounding_span: A JSON-LD document is a serialization of an RDF dataset.

item.name: JSON
item.description: A lightweight, language-independent data interchange format.
item.grounding_span: JSON [RFC8259] is a lightweight, language-independent data interchange format.

item.name: IRI dereferencing
item.description: Using an IRI to retrieve a definition or representation of the term it denotes.

item.name: Croissant metadata format
item.description: A metadata vocabulary/format that describes ML datasets to simplify their use across ML frameworks.
item.grounding_span: The Croissant metadata format simplifies how data is used by ML models.

item.name: JSON-LD encoding
item.description: The RDF syntax in which Croissant metadata is expressed.
item.grounding_span: Croissant metadata is encoded in JSON-LD.

item.name: Dataset discoverability
item.description: Ability for dataset search engines and users to find datasets via their attached metadata.
item.grounding_span: Once a dataset has Croissant metadata attached to it, dataset search engines can parse this metadata, allowing users to find and use the datasets they need no matter where these datasets have been published

item.name: Portability
item.description: The property that a standardized dataset description can be loaded and interpreted identically across ML tools.
item.grounding_span: All this leads to increased portability and reproducibility in the entire ML ecosystem.

item.name: Reproducibility
item.description: The ability to reliably reproduce dataset loading and use through standardized metadata.
item.grounding_span: All this leads to increased portability and reproducibility in the entire ML ecosystem.

item.name: Responsible AI (RAI)
item.description: The practice of exploring, understanding, managing, and assessing the impacts of AI, operationalized via dataset documentation.
item.grounding_span: One of the main instruments to operationalise responsible AI (RAI) is dataset documentation.

item.name: Dataset documentation
item.description: Machine-readable metadata capturing how a dataset was created, processed, and enriched.
item.grounding_span: One of the main instruments to operationalise responsible AI (RAI) is dataset documentation.

item.name: Standardization of dataset description and semantics
item.description: A common vocabulary and semantics for describing ML datasets, whose absence hinders dataset use.
item.grounding_span: a lack of standardization in the description and semantics of ML datasets has made it increasingly difficult for researchers and practitioners to explore, understand, and use all but a small fraction of popular datasets.

item.name: Machine learning dataset
item.description: A collection of data used to train and evaluate machine learning models.
item.grounding_span: Datasets are the basis of machine learning (ML).

item.name: Distribution property
item.description: The property that describes the resources contained in a dataset, holding FileObject or FileSet values in Croissant.

item.name: Resource
item.description: A description of how dataset data is organized; Croissant defines FileObject and FileSet.
item.grounding_span: Croissant defines two types of resources:

item.name: FileObject
item.description: Croissant class representing individual files that are part of a dataset.
item.grounding_span: `FileObject` is the Croissant class used to represent individual files that are part of a dataset.

item.name: FileSet
item.description: Croissant class describing homogeneous collections of files, e.g. a directory of images.
item.grounding_span: `FileSet` is a class that describes such collections of files.

item.name: RecordSet
item.description: A description of a set of structured records and their fields, obtained from one or more data sources.
item.grounding_span: A `RecordSet` describes a set of structured records obtained from one or more data sources (typically a file or set of files) and the structure of these records, expressed as a set of fields (e.g., the columns of a table).

item.name: Field
item.description: A data element of a RecordSet, e.g. a column, nested structure, or nested RecordSet.
item.grounding_span: A `Field` is part of a `RecordSet`.

item.name: DataSource
item.description: The class describing data that can be extracted and transformed from files to populate a RecordSet.
item.grounding_span: `DataSource` is the class describing the data that can be extracted from files to populate a `RecordSet`.

item.name: Extract
item.description: Specifies which subset of a source (column, fileProperty, jsonPath) to extract.
item.grounding_span: The `Extract` class can be used to specify how to do that, depending on the type of the data.

item.name: Transform
item.description: Simple transformations (delimiter, regex, jsonQuery) applied to extracted source data.
item.grounding_span: Croissant supports a few simple transformations that can be applied on the source data:

item.name: Format
item.description: A format string used to parse values from a DataSource into a target data type.
item.grounding_span: A format string used to parse the values coming from a `DataSource`.

item.name: DataType
item.description: The type of values expected for a Field or RecordSet; atomic or semantic.
item.grounding_span: Croissant supports two kinds of data types: simple, atomic data types such as integers and strings, and semantic data types, which convey more meaning and can be structured

item.name: Hierarchical data
item.description: Tree-structured data represented via nested fields and nested records.

item.name: Nested field (subField)
item.description: Fields nested inside other fields to group them logically.
item.grounding_span: `Field`s may be nested inside other fields, via the `subField` property

item.name: Nested record
item.description: Multiple records nested inside a single record to represent hierarchical or denormalized data.
item.grounding_span: Croissant also supports nesting (multiple) records inside a single record.

item.name: Categorical data / enumeration
item.description: Data with a finite set of values, marked via the sc:Enumeration dataType on a RecordSet.
item.grounding_span: Croissant represents that information by using the [sc:Enumeration](https://schema.org/Enumeration) class from [schema.org](https://schema.org), as a `dataType` on `RecordSet`s that hold categorical data.

item.name: Data split
item.description: Partitioning of data into subsets (train, validation, test) via the cr:Split dataType.
item.grounding_span: The Croissant format allows for the data to be split arbitrarily into one or multiple splits, which for example allows dataset consumers to load a specific split.

item.name: Label data
item.description: Data identified as labels via the cr:Label class, applying to the record they are defined in.
item.grounding_span: In Croissant, we identify label data using the class `cr:Label`.

item.name: Bounding box
item.description: A 4-float array interpreted as a rectangle outlining objects in images or videos.
item.grounding_span: Croissant defines the type `cr:BoundingBox` that interprets any 4-float array as a bounding box.

item.verbatim_text: Data Catalog Vocabulary - United States. The federal metadata standard that data.gov requires for all published datasets. DCAT-US defines which metadata fields are required (such as title, description, modified date, and keywords) and what formats are acceptable for each field. Harvest validation errors occur when dataset metadata does not conform to the DCAT-US schema.
item.grounding_span: Data Catalog Vocabulary - United States. The federal metadata standard that data.gov requires for all published datasets. DCAT-US defines which metadata fields are required (such as title, description, modified date, and keywords) and what formats are acceptable for each field. Harvest validation errors occur when dataset metadata does not conform to the DCAT-US schema.

item.verbatim_text: A DCAT-US metadata field describing how often a dataset is updated. Must use ISO 8601 duration codes in repeating interval format (such as R/P1W for weekly, R/P1M for monthly, R/P1Y for annual) or the literal value 'irregular' for datasets that are no longer updated. Plain English descriptions like 'Weekly' or 'Monthly' are not accepted and cause validation failures.

item.verbatim_text: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the email address for the dataset contact. Must be formatted as a single mailto: URI (for example, mailto:contact@agency.gov) with no extra text, no subject lines, no multiple addresses, and no trailing spaces. Common validation failures include appended subject lines, multiple email addresses in one field, or invisible Unicode characters from copy-pasting.

item.verbatim_text: A harvest error that occurs when a metadata field value does not conform to the DCAT-US schema requirements. The harvester can read the record, but a specific field value is formatted incorrectly, contains an unacceptable value, or is missing when required. item.name: RDF Data Cube vocabulary
item.description: A W3C vocabulary for publishing multi-dimensional data such as statistics on the web in RDF.
item.grounding_span: The Data Cube vocabulary provides a means to do this using the W3C RDF (Resource Description Framework) standard.

item.name: multi-dimensional data publication
item.description: Publication of multi-dimensional data such as statistics on the web so it can be linked to related data.
item.grounding_span: to be able to publish multi-dimensional data, such as statistics, on the web in such a way that it can be linked to related data sets and concepts

item.name: statistical data
item.description: Observed values organized along dimensions with associated metadata, foundational to policy.
item.grounding_span: Statistical data is a foundation for policy prediction, planning and adjustments

item.name: cube model
item.description: A statistical data set modeled as a multi-dimensional space indexed by dimensions.
item.grounding_span: We can think of the statistical data set as a multi-dimensional space, or hyper-cube, indexed by those dimensions.

item.name: component
item.description: Collective term for the dimensions, attributes and measures of a cube.
item.grounding_span: A cube is organized according to a set of *dimensions*, *attributes* and *measures*. We collectively call these *components*.

item.name: dimension component
item.description: Component that identifies observations; a full set of dimension values identifies one observation.
item.grounding_span: The *dimension* components serve to identify the observations.

item.name: attribute component
item.description: Component that qualifies and interprets observed values, e.g. units and status.
item.grounding_span: The *attribute* components allow us to qualify and interpret the observed value(s).

item.name: measure component
item.description: Component representing the phenomenon being observed.
item.grounding_span: The *measure* components represent the phenomenon being observed.

item.name: observation
item.description: A single data point in the cube with associated measured values.
item.grounding_span: Each observation is represented as an instance of type `qb:Observation`.

item.name: DataSet
item.description: A collection of statistical data conforming to a defined structure.
item.grounding_span: A DataSet is a collection of statistical data that corresponds to a defined structure.

item.name: Data Structure Definition
item.description: Defines the dimensions, attributes and measures used by one or more datasets.
item.grounding_span: A `qb:DataStructureDefinition` defines the structure of one or more datasets.

item.name: ComponentSpecification
item.description: Qualifies the use of a component property within a DSD.
item.grounding_span: In the simplest case the `qb:ComponentSpecification` simply references the corresponding `qb:ComponentProperty`

item.name: ComponentProperty
item.description: Abstract RDF property superclass for dimensions, attributes and measures.
item.grounding_span: Each is an instance of the abstract `qb:ComponentProperty` class, which in turn has sub-classes `qb:DimensionProperty`, `qb:AttributeProperty` and `qb:MeasureProperty`.

item.name: ComponentSet
item.description: Abstract class of things that reference one or more ComponentProperties.
item.grounding_span: Abstract class of things which reference one or more ComponentProperties

item.name: Attachable
item.description: Abstract superclass for everything that can have attributes and dimensions.
item.grounding_span: Abstract superclass for everything that can have attributes and dimensions.

item.name: slice
item.description: A subset of a DataSet formed by fixing a subset of dimension values.
item.grounding_span: We call such a selection a *slice* through the cube.

item.name: SliceKey
item.description: Lists the dimension component properties fixed in the corresponding slices.
item.grounding_span: This is done by creating a `qb:SliceKey` to list the component properties (which must be dimensions) which will be fixed in the slice.

item.name: ObservationGroup
item.description: An arbitrary group of observations; a Slice is a special case.
item.grounding_span: A `qb:ObservationGroup` can contain an arbitrary collection of observations.

item.name: code list
item.description: A (possibly hierarchical) set of coded values for a dimension.
item.grounding_span: In statistical data sets it is common for values to be encoded using some (possibly hierarchical) code list

item.name: SKOS concept scheme
item.description: The overall set of admissible coded values represented in SKOS.
item.grounding_span: the overall set of admissible values using `skos:ConceptScheme` or `skos:Collection`.

item.name: skos:Concept coded value
item.description: An individual code value represented as a SKOS concept.
item.grounding_span: representing the individual code values using `skos:Concept`

item.name: HierarchicalCodeList
item.description: A generalized hierarchy of coding concepts defined by roots and a parent-child property.
item.grounding_span: The Data Cube vocabulary supports this situation through the `qb:HierarchicalCodeList` class.

item.name: measure dimension approach
item.description: Multiple-measure approach adding a dimension whose value indicates the measure conveyed.
item.grounding_span: This *measure dimension* approach is the one supported by the SDMX information model.

item.name: multi-measure approach
item.description: Approach where a single observation carries values for multiple measures.
item.grounding_span: In the second approach a single observation can provide values for multiple different measures.

item.name: qb:measureType magic dimension
item.description: Distinguished measure dimension with an implicit code list of the DSD's measures.
item.grounding_span: For use within the Data Cube vocabulary we provide a single distinguished component for this purpose -- `qb:measureType`.

item.name: normalized representation
item.description: Representation attaching every component value to each individual observation.
item.grounding_span: By default the values of all of the components will be attached to each individual observation, this is called the *normalized* representation.

item.name: abbreviated representation
item.description: Representation attaching component properties at higher levels (DataSet/Slice) to reduce redundancy.
item.grounding_span: To address this the Data Cube vocabulary supports a notion of an *abbreviated* format in which component properties may be *attached* to other levels in the Data Cube.

item.name: component attachment level
item.description: The level (DataSet, Slice, Observation, MeasureProperty) at which a component is attached.
item.grounding_span: the `qb:componentAttachment` property of the specification should reference the class corresponding to the attachment level

item.name: well-formed cube
item.description: An RDF graph of DataSets that passes all defined integrity checks.
item.grounding_span: A well-formed RDF Data Cube is an a RDF graph describing one or more instances of `qb:DataSet` for which each of the integrity checks defined here passes.

item.name: integrity constraint
item.description: A constraint an RDF Data Cube should conform to, expressed in prose and SPARQL ASK.
item.grounding_span: An instance of an RDF Data Cube should conform to a set of integrity constraints which we define in this section.

item.name: linked data
item.description: An approach to publishing data on the web that links datasets through common concepts.
item.grounding_span: *Linked data* is an approach to publishing data on the web, enabling datasets to be linked together through references to common concepts.

item.name: RDF
item.description: W3C standard for representing information describing entities and concepts.
item.grounding_span: RDF [RDF-PRIMER] provides a standard for the representation of the information that describes those entities and concepts

item.name: HTTP URI naming
item.description: Use of dereferenceable HTTP URIs to name entities and concepts.
item.grounding_span: The approach [LOD] recommends use of HTTP URIs to name the entities and concepts so that consumers of the data can look-up those URIs to get more information

item.name: content-oriented guidelines
item.description: SDMX cross-domain concepts, code lists and categories reusable across datasets.
item.grounding_span: The SDMX standard includes a set of *content oriented guidelines* (COG) [COG]

item.name: aggregation over hierarchies
item.description: Publishing aggregated statistics for non-leaf concepts of a code hierarchy.
item.grounding_span: The use of SKOS, or non-SKOS, hierarchies makes it possible to publish aggregated statistics for the non-leaf concepts in the hierarchy.

item.name: normalization algorithm
item.description: A SPARQL Update transformation that normalizes an abbreviated Data Cube.
item.grounding_span: We define these notions by means of a transformation algorithm which can normalize an abbreviated Data Cube.

item.name: conformance
item.description: Criteria under which a data interchange is conformant with Data Cube.
item.grounding_span: A data interchange, however that interchange occurs, is conformant with Data Cube if:

item.name: coded property
item.description: Superclass of all coded component properties.
item.grounding_span: Superclass of all coded component properties.

item.name: structural metadata
item.description: Metadata needed to interpret a located observation, provided as attributes.
item.grounding_span: Having located an observation, we need certain metadata in order to be able to interpret it.

item.name: reference metadata
item.description: Metadata describing the dataset as a whole such as categorization and publisher.
item.grounding_span: This is metadata that describes the dataset as a whole, such as categorization of the dataset, its publisher, and a SPARQL endpoint where it can be accessed.

item.name: component order
item.description: Integer ordering of components to guide presentation.
item.grounding_span: The components may be ordered by giving an integer value for `qb:order`.

item.name: required vs optional components
item.description: Attributes may be optional or required; only attributes may be optional.
item.grounding_span: Attributes may be declared as optional or required.

item.name: Data Cube integrity constraints
item.owner: W3C Government Linked Data Working Group
item.method: SPARQL ASK queries evaluating well-formedness of an RDF Data Cube graph
item.grounding_span: An instance of an RDF Data Cube should conform to a set of integrity constraints which we define in this section.

item.text: The RDF graph must be consistent under RDF D-entailment [RDF-MT] using a datatype map containing all the datatypes used within the graph.
item.grounding_span: The RDF graph must be consistent under RDF D-entailment [RDF-MT] using a datatype map containing all the datatypes used within the graph.

item.text: Every qb:Observation has exactly one associated qb:DataSet.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:Observation` has exactly one associated `qb:DataSet`.

item.text: Every qb:DataSet has exactly one associated qb:DataStructureDefinition.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:DataSet` has exactly one associated `qb:DataStructureDefinition`.

item.text: Every qb:DataStructureDefinition must include at least one declared measure.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:DataStructureDefinition` must include at least one declared measure.

item.text: Every dimension declared in a qb:DataStructureDefinition must have a declared rdfs:range.
item.grounding_span: Every dimension declared in a `qb:DataStructureDefinition` must have a declared `rdfs:range`.

item.text: Every dimension with range skos:Concept must have a qb:codeList.
item.grounding_span: Every dimension with range `skos:Concept` must have a `qb:codeList`.

item.text: The only components of a qb:DataStructureDefinition that may be marked as optional using qb:componentRequired are attributes.
item.grounding_span: The only components of a `qb:DataStructureDefinition` that may be marked as optional, using `qb:componentRequired` are attributes.

item.text: Every qb:SliceKey must be associated with a qb:DataStructureDefinition.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:SliceKey` must be associated with a `qb:DataStructureDefinition`.

item.text: Every qb:componentProperty on a qb:SliceKey must also be declared as a qb:component of the associated qb:DataStructureDefinition.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:componentProperty` on a `qb:SliceKey` must also be declared as a `qb:component` of the associated `qb:DataStructureDefinition`.

item.text: Each qb:Slice must have exactly one associated qb:sliceStructure.
item.grounding_span: Each `qb:Slice` must have exactly one associated `qb:sliceStructure`.

item.text: Every qb:Slice must have a value for every dimension declared in its qb:sliceStructure.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:Slice` must have a value for every dimension declared in its `qb:sliceStructure`.

item.text: Every qb:Observation has a value for each dimension declared in its associated qb:DataStructureDefinition.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:Observation` has a value for each dimension declared in its associated `qb:DataStructureDefinition`.

item.text: No two qb:Observations in the same qb:DataSet may have the same value for all dimensions.
item.grounding_span: No two `qb:Observation`s in the same `qb:DataSet` may have the same value for all dimensions.

item.text: Every qb:Observation has a value for each declared attribute that is marked as required.
item.grounding_span: Every `qb:Observation` has a value for each declared attribute that is marked as required.

item.text: In a qb:DataSet which does not use a Measure dimension each qb:Observation must have a value for every declared measure.
item.grounding_span: In a `qb:DataSet` which does not use a Measure dimension then each individual `qb:Observation` must have a value for every declared measure.

item.text: In a qb:DataSet which uses a Measure dimension each qb:Observation must have a value for the measure corresponding to its qb:measureType.
item.grounding_span: In a `qb:DataSet` which uses a Measure dimension then each `qb:Observation` must have a value for the measure corresponding to its given `qb:measureType`.

item.text: In a measure-dimension qb:DataSet each qb:Observation must only have a value for one measure.
item.grounding_span: In a `qb:DataSet` which uses a Measure dimension then each `qb:Observation` must only have a value for one measure (by IC-15 this will be the measure corresponding to its `qb:measureType`).

item.text: In a measure-dimension cube every populated non-measure dimension point must have observations for each declared measure.
item.grounding_span: In a `qb:DataSet` which uses a Measure dimension then if there is a Observation for some combination of non-measure dimensions then there must be other Observations with the same non-measure dimension values for each of the declared measures.

item.text: If a DataSet D has a qb:slice S with a qb:observation O then O's qb:dataSet must be D.
item.grounding_span: If a `qb:DataSet` D has a `qb:slice` S, and S has an `qb:observation` O, then the `qb:dataSet` corresponding to O must be D.

item.text: If a dimension property has a qb:codeList, its value on every qb:Observation must be in the code list.
item.grounding_span: If a dimension property has a `qb:codeList`, then the value of the dimension property on every `qb:Observation` must be in the code list.

item.text: For a HierarchicalCodeList with a non-blank parentChildProperty, dimension values must be reachable from a hierarchy root along that property.
item.grounding_span: If a dimension property has a `qb:HierarchicalCodeList` with a non-blank `qb:parentChildProperty` then the value of that dimension property on every `qb:Observation` must be reachable from a root of the hierarchy using zero or more hops along the `qb:parentChildProperty` links.

item.text: For a HierarchicalCodeList with an inverse parentChildProperty, dimension values must be reachable from a hierarchy root along the inverse property.
item.grounding_span: If a dimension property has a `qb:HierarchicalCodeList` with an inverse `qb:parentChildProperty` then the value of that dimension property on every `qb:Observation` must be reachable from a root of the hierarchy using zero or more hops along the inverse `qb:parentChildProperty` links.

item.name: OpenAPI Specification (OAS)
item.description: A standard, programming language-agnostic interface description for HTTP APIs.
item.grounding_span: The OpenAPI Specification (OAS) defines a standard, programming language-agnostic interface description for HTTP APIs

item.name: OpenAPI Description (OAD)
item.description: A formal description of an API surface and semantics, possibly across multiple documents.
item.grounding_span: An **OpenAPI Description** (**OAD**) formally describes the surface of an API and its semantics.

item.name: entry document
item.description: The document containing the OpenAPI Object where parsing of a multi-document OAD begins.
item.grounding_span: the document containing the OpenAPI Object where parsing begins is known as that OAD’s **entry document**

item.name: embedding format
item.description: Another format in which an OpenAPI Object may be embedded.
item.grounding_span: An OpenAPI Object *MAY* be embedded in another format, called the **embedding format**

item.name: multi-document OAD
item.description: An OAD distributed across multiple connected documents.
item.grounding_span: be distributed across multiple documents that are connected by various fields using URI references and implicit connections

item.name: undefined behavior
item.description: Situations likely to produce outcomes contradicting the specification.
item.grounding_span: Behavior described as *undefined* is likely, at least in some circumstances, to result in outcomes that contradict the specification.

item.name: implementation-defined behavior
item.description: Ambiguous requirements where implementations choose among compliant approaches.
item.grounding_span: Behavior described as *implementation-defined* allows implementations to choose which of several different-but-compliant approaches to a requirement to implement.

item.name: OAS versioning and feature set
item.description: major.minor.patch versioning where major.minor designates the feature set.
item.grounding_span: The `major`.`minor` portion of the version string (for example `3.1`) *SHALL* designate the OAS feature set.

item.name: deprecation
item.description: Fields/features marked Deprecated remain usable but should be replaced.
item.grounding_span: Certain fields or features may be marked **Deprecated**.

item.name: specification extensions
item.description: Patterned fields prefixed by x- to extend the specification.
item.grounding_span: The extensions properties are implemented as patterned fields that are always prefixed by `x-`.

item.name: fixed and patterned fields
item.description: Two kinds of OAS object fields: declared-name and declared-pattern.
item.grounding_span: OAS Objects expose two types of fields: *fixed fields*, which have a declared name, and *patterned fields*, which have a declared pattern for the field name.

item.name: case sensitivity
item.description: OAS field names are case-sensitive except where noted.
item.grounding_span: All field names in the specification are **case-sensitive**.

item.name: CommonMark rich text
item.description: description fields support CommonMark markdown for rich text.
item.grounding_span: Throughout the specification `description` fields are noted as supporting [CommonMark] markdown formatting.

item.name: OpenAPI Object
item.description: The root object of an OpenAPI Description.
item.grounding_span: This is the root object of the OpenAPI Description.

item.name: $self and base URI
item.description: Self-assigned URI of a document that serves as its base URI.
item.grounding_span: The `$self` field provides the self-assigned URI of this document, which also serves as its base URI in accordance with [RFC3986] Section 5.1.1.

item.name: retrieval URI
item.description: The most common base URI source when $self/$id is missing or relative.
item.grounding_span: The most common base URI source that is used in the event of a missing or relative `$self` (in the OpenAPI Object) and (for Schema Object) `$id` is the retrieval URI.

item.name: relative references (URIs vs URLs)
item.description: Reference URIs resolved as identifiers, contrasted with API URLs.
item.grounding_span: are resolved as *identifiers*, and described by this specification as ***URIs***, in contrast with API URLs.

item.name: resolving implicit connections
item.description: Non-URI-based connections between parts of an OAD.
item.grounding_span: Several features of this specification require resolution of non-URI-based connections to some other part of the OpenAPI Description (OAD).

item.name: webhooks
item.description: Incoming requests initiated by the API provider that a consumer may implement.
item.grounding_span: The incoming webhooks that *MAY* be received as part of this API

item.name: Info Object
item.description: Metadata about the API.
item.grounding_span: The object provides metadata about the API.

item.name: Server Object
item.description: Connectivity information for a target host.
item.grounding_span: An object representing a Server.

item.name: server URL templating and variables
item.description: Substitution of named variables in a server URL template.
item.grounding_span: An object representing a Server Variable for server URL template substitution.

item.name: Components Object
item.description: Holder of reusable objects referenced from elsewhere.
item.grounding_span: Holds a set of reusable objects for different aspects of the OAS.

item.name: path templating
item.description: Curly-brace template expressions marking replaceable URL path sections.
item.grounding_span: Path templating refers to the usage of template expressions, delimited by curly braces (`{}`), to mark a section of a URL path as replaceable using path parameters.

item.name: Path Item Object
item.description: The operations available on a single path.
item.grounding_span: Describes the operations available on a single path.

item.name: Operation Object
item.description: A single API operation on a path.
item.grounding_span: Describes a single API operation on a path.

item.name: parameter locations
item.description: Five parameter locations specified by the in field.
item.grounding_span: There are five possible parameter locations specified by the `in` field:

item.name: style-based serialization
item.description: Style values that define how parameter values are serialized.
item.grounding_span: In order to support common ways of serializing simple parameters, a set of `style` values are defined.

item.name: URL percent-encoding
item.description: Percent-decoding/encoding rules for API URLs and form-urlencoded content.
item.grounding_span: All API URLs *MUST* successfully parse and percent-decode using [RFC3986] rules.

item.name: Request Body Object
item.description: A single request body with content keyed by media type.
item.grounding_span: Describes a single request body.

item.name: Media Type Object
item.description: Describes content structured according to a media type key.
item.grounding_span: Each Media Type Object describes content structured in accordance with the media type identified by its key.

item.name: sequential media type
item.description: A media type consisting of a repeating structure with no envelope.
item.grounding_span: a *sequential media type* is defined as any media type that consists of a repeating structure, without any sort of header, footer, envelope, or other metadata in addition to the sequence.

item.name: streaming content and itemSchema
item.description: itemSchema applies per stream item to support streaming.
item.grounding_span: The `itemSchema` field is provided to support streaming use cases for sequential media types

item.name: Server-Sent Events
item.description: Handling of parsed text/event-stream event data.
item.grounding_span: For `text/event-stream`, implementations *MUST* work with event data after it has been parsed according to the `text/event-stream` specification

item.name: Encoding Object
item.description: A single encoding definition applied to a single value.
item.grounding_span: A single encoding definition applied to a single value

item.name: encoding by position
item.description: Multipart data modeled as an ordered array of parts.
item.grounding_span: Data for these media types are modeled as an array, with one item per part, in order.

item.name: binary data (raw and encoded)
item.description: OAS describes raw (unencoded) or encoded binary data.
item.grounding_span: The OAS can describe either *raw* or *encoded* binary data.

item.name: Responses Object
item.description: Container mapping HTTP response codes to expected responses.
item.grounding_span: A container for the expected responses of an operation.

item.name: Callback Object
item.description: Out-of-band callbacks keyed by a runtime expression URL.
item.grounding_span: A map of possible out-of band callbacks related to the parent operation.

item.name: runtime expression
item.description: Values derived from information available only within an actual HTTP message.
item.grounding_span: Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.

item.name: Example Object
item.description: Groups internal/external example values with summary/description metadata.
item.grounding_span: An object grouping an internal or external example value with basic `summary` and `description` metadata.

item.name: Link Object (design-time links)
item.description: A possible design-time link between a response and other operations.
item.grounding_span: The Link Object represents a possible design-time link for a response.

item.name: Header Object

item.name: Tag Object and tag hierarchy

item.name: Reference Object
item.description: Object to reference other components via a $ref URI.
item.grounding_span: A simple object to allow referencing other components in the OpenAPI Description, internally and externally.

item.name: Schema Object
item.description: Defines input and output data types.
item.grounding_span: The Schema Object allows the definition of input and output data types.

item.name: JSON Schema superset (Draft 2020-12)
item.description: The Schema Object is a superset of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12.
item.grounding_span: This object is a superset of the JSON Schema Specification Draft 2020-12.

item.name: data type format
item.description: Optional non-validating format modifier keyword.

item.name: data catalog
item.description: A collection of metadata records describing datasets and data services published on the Web.
item.grounding_span: DCAT is a vocabulary for publishing data catalogs on the Web

item.name: dataset
item.description: A conceptual collection of data published or curated by a single agent.
item.grounding_span: `dcat:Dataset` represents a collection of data, published or curated by a single agent or identifiable community.

item.name: distribution
item.description: An accessible, specific representation of a dataset such as a downloadable file.
item.grounding_span: `dcat:Distribution` represents an accessible form of a dataset such as a downloadable file.

item.name: data service
item.description: A collection of operations accessible through an API providing access to datasets or data processing functions.
item.grounding_span: `dcat:DataService` represents a collection of operations accessible through an interface (API) that provide access to one or more datasets or data processing functions.

item.name: dataset series
item.description: A dataset grouping datasets that are published separately but share characteristics.
item.grounding_span: `dcat:DatasetSeries` is a dataset that represents a collection of datasets that are published separately, but share some characteristics that group them.

item.name: catalog
item.description: A dataset whose members are metadata records describing resources.
item.grounding_span: `dcat:Catalog` represents a catalog, which is a dataset in which each individual item is a metadata record describing some resource

item.name: cataloged resource
item.description: Parent class of datasets, data services and catalogs; any resource describable in a catalog.
item.grounding_span: `dcat:Resource` represents a dataset, a data service or any other resource that may be described by a metadata record in a catalog.

item.name: catalog record
item.description: A metadata record capturing registration information about a resource in the catalog.
item.grounding_span: `dcat:CatalogRecord` represents a metadata record in the catalog, primarily concerning the registration information, such as who added the record and when.

item.name: metadata
item.description: Descriptive information about data resources enabling their sharing and discovery.
item.grounding_span: Sharing data resources among different organizations, researchers, governments and citizens requires the provision of metadata.

item.name: interoperability
item.description: The ability to consume and aggregate metadata across data catalogs.
item.grounding_span: DCAT is an RDF vocabulary designed to facilitate interoperability between data catalogs published on the Web.

item.name: discoverability
item.description: The property of datasets and services being findable.
item.grounding_span: increase the discoverability of datasets and data services

item.name: federated search
item.description: Searching for datasets across catalogs in multiple sites using a common query mechanism.
item.grounding_span: allow federated search for datasets across catalogs in multiple sites

item.name: decentralized publishing
item.description: A decentralized approach to publishing data catalogs.
item.grounding_span: makes it possible to have a decentralized approach to publishing data catalogs

item.name: Linked Data
item.description: A Web-of-data context where resources are linked and annotated collaboratively.
item.grounding_span: in a Linked Data context, blank nodes limit our ability to collaboratively annotate data.

item.name: blank node
item.description: An RDF resource denoted without an explicit IRI.
item.grounding_span: Blank nodes can be used to denote resources without explicitly naming them with an IRI.

item.name: global identifier
item.description: A globally unique identifier recommended for DCAT main class instances.
item.grounding_span: it is recommended that instances of the DCAT main classes have a global identifier, and use of blank nodes is generally discouraged when encoding DCAT in RDF.

item.name: dereferenceable identifier
item.description: Identifiers made actionable via persistent HTTP IRIs.
item.grounding_span: DCAT primarily relies on persistent HTTP IRIs as an effective way of making identifiers actionable.

item.name: versioning
item.description: Describing versions of a resource resulting from revisions in its life-cycle.
item.grounding_span: This section focuses specifically on how to use DCAT to describe versions resulting from a revision - i.e., from changes occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle.

item.name: version chain
item.description: A backward-navigable sequence of resource versions.
item.grounding_span: Property `dcat:previousVersion` is used to build a version chain that can be navigated backward from a given version to the first one.

item.name: version hierarchy
item.description: A structure linking an abstract resource to its versions.
item.grounding_span: property `dcat:hasVersion` can be used to specify a version hierarchy, by linking an abstract resource to its versions.

item.name: resource life-cycle
item.description: The evolution of a resource through workflow statuses, orthogonal to versioning.
item.grounding_span: The life-cycle of a resource is an aspect orthogonal to versioning, and sometimes strictly related.

item.name: backward compatibility
item.description: Preservation of prior term definitions across DCAT versions.
item.grounding_span: DCAT 3 maintains the DCAT namespace as its terms preserve backward compatibility with DCAT 2.

item.name: qualified relation
item.description: An n-ary pattern attaching a role to a relationship between resources.
item.grounding_span: A general method for relating a resource to another resource with a specified role is provided by using the qualified form `dcat:qualifiedRelation`.

item.name: qualified attribution
item.description: An n-ary pattern assigning an agent to a resource with a specified role.
item.grounding_span: A general method for assigning an agent to a resource with a specified role is provided by using the qualified form `prov:qualifiedAttribution` from [PROV-O].

item.name: role
item.description: The function of a resource or agent with respect to another resource.
item.grounding_span: A role is the function of a resource or agent with respect to another resource, in the context of resource attribution or resource relationships.

item.name: data citation
item.description: Referencing data as a first-class output like bibliographic references.
item.grounding_span: Data citation is the practice of referencing data in a similar way as when providing bibliographic references

item.name: license
item.description: A legal document under which a resource is made available.
item.grounding_span: use `dcterms:license` to refer to licenses

item.name: access rights
item.description: Statements about who can access a resource.
item.grounding_span: use `dcterms:accessRights` to express statements concerning only access rights

item.name: ODRL policy
item.description: Rights expressed as a machine-readable ODRL policy.
item.grounding_span: in the particular case when rights are expressed via ODRL policies, it is recommended to use the `odrl:hasPolicy` property

item.name: data quality
item.description: Multi-dimensional characteristics of data described via DQV.
item.grounding_span: The Data Quality Vocabulary (DQV) [VOCAB-DQV] offers common modeling patterns for different aspects of Data Quality.

item.name: quality dimension
item.description: A quality characteristic relevant to the consumer.
item.grounding_span: Each type of quality information can pertain to one or more quality dimensions

item.name: conformance to a standard
item.description: Declaring that a resource conforms to a standard via dcterms:conformsTo.
item.grounding_span: The use of `dcterms:conformsTo` and `dcterms:Standard` is a well-known pattern to represent the conformance to a standard.

item.name: degree of conformance
item.description: The extent (conformant, not conformant, not evaluated) to which a resource meets a standard.
item.grounding_span: Some legal context requires to specify the degree of conformance.

item.name: DCAT profile
item.description: A specification adding constraints on top of DCAT.
item.grounding_span: A **DCAT profile** is a specification for a data catalog that adds additional constraints to DCAT.

item.name: theme taxonomy
item.description: A classification system for the resources in a catalog.
item.grounding_span: A knowledge organization system (KOS) used to classify the resources documented in the catalog

item.name: accrual periodicity
item.description: The frequency at which a dataset is published/updated.
item.grounding_span: The frequency at which a dataset is published.

item.name: temporal coverage
item.description: The temporal period that the dataset covers.
item.grounding_span: The temporal period that the dataset covers.

item.name: temporal resolution
item.description: Minimum time period resolvable in the dataset.
item.grounding_span: Minimum time period resolvable in the dataset.

item.name: spatial coverage
item.description: The geographical area covered by the dataset.
item.grounding_span: The geographical area covered by the dataset.

item.name: spatial resolution
item.description: Minimum spatial separation resolvable in a dataset, in meters.
item.grounding_span: Minimum spatial separation resolvable in a dataset, measured in meters.

item.name: period of time
item.description: An interval of time defined by its start and end.
item.grounding_span: An interval of time that is named or defined by its start and end.

item.name: location
item.description: A spatial region or named place.
item.grounding_span: A spatial region or named place.

item.name: checksum
item.description: A value verifying file contents have not changed.
item.grounding_span: A Checksum is a value that allows to check the integrity of the contents of a file.

item.name: agent
item.description: A person or organization responsible for a resource.
item.grounding_span: published or curated by a single agent

item.name: inverse property
item.description: Optional inverse forms of DCAT properties usable in addition to the primary ones.
item.grounding_span: recognizing that inverses are needed for some use cases, DCAT supports them

item.name: upstream inheritance
item.description: Child dataset property values inherited by the parent dataset series.
item.grounding_span: property values of child datasets are inherited by their parent (the dataset series).

item.name: catalog conformance
item.description: The conditions under which a data catalog conforms to DCAT.
item.grounding_span: A data catalog conforms to DCAT if:
