item.name: Statistical Data and Metadata Exchange (SDMX)
item.description: The initiative that sets standards facilitating the exchange of statistical data and metadata using modern information technology.
item.grounding_span: Statistical Data and Metadata Exchange (SDMX)

item.name: Statistical data
item.description: Sets of often numeric observations which typically have time associated with them.
item.grounding_span: numeric observations which typically have time associated with them.

item.name: Metadata
item.description: The broad category of information describing and qualifying statistical data, split into structural and reference metadata.
item.grounding_span: Statistical Data and Metadata

item.name: Structural metadata
item.description: Concepts used in the description and identification of statistical data and metadata.
item.grounding_span: structural metadata

item.name: Reference metadata
item.description: The larger set of concepts that describe and qualify statistical data sets and processing more generally.
item.grounding_span: reference metadata

item.name: Exchange of statistical data and metadata
item.description: The transfer of statistical data and metadata between counterparties, the primary focus of SDMX.
item.grounding_span: exchange of statistical data and metadata

item.name: Data dissemination
item.description: Supply of data and metadata to end users, increasingly published on websites.
item.grounding_span: dissemination of data

item.name: Process pattern
item.description: One of the basic patterns for exchanging statistical data and metadata.
item.grounding_span: three basic process patterns

item.name: Bilateral exchange
item.description: An exchange where all aspects are agreed between counterparties.
item.grounding_span: Bilateral exchange

item.name: Gateway exchange
item.description: An organized set of bilateral exchanges using a single known format and process.
item.grounding_span: Gateway exchange

item.name: Data-sharing exchange
item.description: Open, standard formats and process patterns allowing any counterparty to use another's data.
item.grounding_span: Data-sharing exchange

item.name: Process automation
item.description: Automated processes SDMX supports: batch exchange, internet provision, generic processes, presentation/transformation.
item.grounding_span: automated processes

item.name: Data cube
item.description: A multi-dimensional coordinate system of concepts describing statistical data.
item.grounding_span: multi-dimensional co-ordinate system

item.name: Data Set
item.description: A collection of similar data sharing a structure covering a fixed period of time.
item.grounding_span: Data Set

item.name: Data Structure Definition
item.description: Structural metadata describing how concepts associate with measures, dimensions and attributes of a data cube.
item.grounding_span: Data Structure Definition (DSD, also known as Key Family in Version 2.0)

item.name: Code list
item.description: An enumerated set of codes used in the representation of dimensions, attributes and other structural parts.
item.grounding_span: Code list

item.name: Value list
item.description: A version 3.0 construct similar to a code list whose items need not conform to SDMX identifiable-object rules.
item.grounding_span: Value list

item.name: Organisation Scheme
item.description: A scheme defining organisations and organisation structure (agency, provider, consumer, unit).
item.grounding_span: Organisation Scheme

item.name: Category Scheme and Categorisation
item.description: A hierarchy of categories, with categorisation linking a category to an identifiable object.
item.grounding_span: Category Scheme and Categorisation

item.name: Concept Scheme
item.description: A maintained list of concepts used in data and metadata structure definitions.
item.grounding_span: Concept Scheme

item.name: Metadata Set
item.description: A set of reference metadata pertaining to an object within the SDMX view of statistical exchange.
item.grounding_span: Metadata Set

item.name: Metadata Structure Definition
item.description: Structural metadata describing how a reference metadata set is organized and represented.
item.grounding_span: Metadata Structure Definition

item.name: Dataflow Definition
item.description: Identifies the DSD by which data sets are reported or disseminated; can be categorised and constrained.
item.grounding_span: Dataflow Definition

item.name: Metadataflow Definition
item.description: Describes, categorises and constrains metadata sets, analogous to a dataflow definition.
item.grounding_span: Metadataflow Definition

item.name: Data Provider
item.description: An organization which produces data.
item.grounding_span: Data Provider

item.name: Metadata Provider
item.description: An organization which produces reference metadata.
item.grounding_span: Metadata Provider

item.name: Provision Agreement
item.description: Information describing how data/metadata sets are provided by a provider, including source URL.
item.grounding_span: Provision Agreement

item.name: Constraint
item.description: Describes a subset of a data or metadata source and may give scheduled release information.
item.grounding_span: Constraint

item.name: Structure Map
item.description: Describes mapping between DSDs or dataflows to transform a data set into a different structure.
item.grounding_span: Structure Map

item.name: Representation Map
item.description: Describes mappings between source and target values restricted to code lists, value lists or types.
item.grounding_span: Representation Map

item.name: Item Scheme Map
item.description: Describes mapping rules between item schemes other than code lists and value lists.
item.grounding_span: Item Scheme Map

item.name: Reporting Taxonomy
item.description: Links a number of cube or dataflow definitions that together form a complete report.
item.grounding_span: Reporting Taxonomy

item.name: Process
item.description: A way to model statistical processes as a set of interconnected process steps.
item.grounding_span: The process class provides a way to model statistical processes as a set

item.name: Hierarchy
item.description: Describes complex code hierarchies principally for data discovery, referencing codes from code lists.
item.grounding_span: Describes complex code hierarchies

item.name: Hierarchy Association
item.description: Links a hierarchy to something that needs it, such as a dimension, possibly in a given context.
item.grounding_span: Hierarchy Association

item.name: Transformation Scheme
item.description: A set of VTL transformations meant to be executed together to produce results.
item.grounding_span: Transformation Scheme

item.name: SDMX Registry
item.description: An application maintaining and storing structural metadata and provisioning information for querying; it does not store the data itself.
item.grounding_span: registry services

item.name: RESTful web services
item.description: The web service style SDMX 3.0 standardised on, with five resources (structure, data, schema, availability, metadata).
item.grounding_span: RESTful web services

item.name: Semantic Versioning
item.description: The three-number versioning standard adopted for structural metadata artefacts.
item.grounding_span: Semantic Versioning

item.name: Microdata
item.description: A data type newly supported in version 3.0, aided by multiple measures and array-valued attributes.
item.grounding_span: microdata

item.name: Geospatial data
item.description: A data type newly supported in version 3.0.
item.grounding_span: geospatial data

item.name: Validation and Transformation Language (VTL)
item.description: A standard calculation language for validating and transforming SDMX data.
item.grounding_span: Validation and Transformation Language (VTL)

item.name: Concept role
item.description: A particular context given to a concept for systematic interpretation by machine processing and visualization tools.
item.grounding_span: concept role

item.name: Time series
item.description: Slices of the data cube, identified by a series key of dimension values except time.
item.grounding_span: time series

item.name: Group
item.description: A lower-level component of a data set based on degrees of similarity.
item.grounding_span: made up of one or more lower-level

item.name: Series
item.description: A cluster within a group that has a key and one or more observations.
item.grounding_span: Each series or section has a

item.name: Observation
item.description: A data point combining the time of the observation and its value.
item.grounding_span: the time of the observation, and the value of the observation

item.name: Attribute
item.description: Descriptive metadata attached at any level of the data structure.
item.grounding_span: metadata may be attached at any level of this structure as descriptive

item.name: Series key
item.description: The values for all dimensions specified by the key family except time.
item.grounding_span: dimensions specified by the key family except time

item.name: SOAP web services
item.description: A web services API deprecated in version 3.0 in favour of REST.
item.grounding_span: SOAP web services

item.name: Backward compatibility
item.description: The degree to which a version works with implementations of earlier versions.
item.grounding_span: backward-compatible

item.name: Breaking changes
item.description: Changes where version 3.0 is not backwardly compatible with earlier versions.
item.grounding_span: breaking changes

item.name: Transmission format
item.description: A syntax-bound expression of the SDMX information model (SDMX-ML, SDMX-JSON, SDMX-CSV, SDMX-EDI).
item.grounding_span: transmission formats

item.name: Data provisioning
item.description: Metadata about the content, form, scheduling and mechanism of a data provider's output.
item.grounding_span: data provisioning

item.name: Classification schemes
item.description: Schemes for organizing and managing the exchange and dissemination of data and metadata.
item.grounding_span: classification schemes

item.name: GSIM
item.description: A statistical community/standard to which VTL was intended to be applicable.
item.grounding_span: GSIM

item.name: DDI
item.description: A data documentation community/standard to which VTL was intended to be applicable.
item.grounding_span: DDI

item.name: FAIR Data Principles
item.description: A concise, domain-independent set of guiding principles that render research objects Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable for both machines and people.
item.grounding_span: FAIR Data Principles

item.name: Findability
item.description: The property that (meta)data can be located, via unique persistent identifiers, rich metadata, and indexing in a searchable resource.
item.grounding_span: To be Findable:

item.name: Accessibility
item.description: The property that (meta)data are retrievable by their identifier using an open, standardized communications protocol, with metadata remaining available even when data are not.
item.grounding_span: To be Accessible:

item.name: Interoperability
item.description: The ability of data or tools from non-cooperating resources to integrate or work together with minimal effort.
item.grounding_span: To be Interoperable:

item.name: Reusability
item.description: The property that (meta)data are richly described, licensed, provenance-tracked, and meet community standards so they can be reused by others.
item.grounding_span: To be Reusable:

item.name: Machine-actionability
item.description: A continuum of states wherein a digital object provides increasingly detailed information enabling an autonomous computational agent to identify, assess, and act on it.
item.grounding_span: toward machine-actionability

item.name: Good data management
item.description: The practices of collection, annotation, archival, and long-term care of digital assets that act as a conduit to knowledge discovery and reuse.
item.grounding_span: good data management

item.name: Data stewardship
item.description: The long-term care of valuable digital assets so they can be discovered and reused for downstream investigations.
item.grounding_span: data stewardship

item.name: Scholarly digital objects
item.description: All research outputs — from data to algorithms, tools, and workflows — that should become first-class citizens in the publication ecosystem.
item.grounding_span: scholarly digital objects

item.name: Research objects
item.description: All components of the research process (data and non-data assets) to which the FAIR principles apply.
item.grounding_span: all research objects should be Findable

item.name: Rich metadata
item.description: Descriptive information about a digital object, richly described with a plurality of accurate and relevant attributes.
item.grounding_span: rich metadata

item.name: Globally unique and persistent identifier
item.description: An identifier assigned to (meta)data that is globally unique and persistent.
item.grounding_span: globally unique and persistent identi ﬁer

item.name: Digital Object Identifier (DOI)
item.description: A code used to permanently and stably identify (usually digital) objects, providing a standard mechanism for metadata retrieval and access.
item.grounding_span: a code used to permanently and stably identify (usually digital) objects

item.name: Standardized communications protocol
item.description: An open, free, and universally implementable protocol by which (meta)data are retrieved by their identifier.
item.grounding_span: standardized communications protocol

item.name: Knowledge representation language
item.description: A formal, accessible, shared, and broadly applicable language for representing knowledge.
item.grounding_span: language for knowledge representation

item.name: Vocabularies and ontologies
item.description: Controlled vocabularies that themselves follow FAIR principles, used to annotate (meta)data.
item.grounding_span: use vocabularies that follow FAIR principles

item.name: Qualified references
item.description: Explicit, qualified links from (meta)data to other (meta)data.
item.grounding_span: references to other (meta)data

item.name: Data usage license
item.description: A clear and accessible license governing reuse of released (meta)data.
item.grounding_span: clear and accessible data usage license

item.name: Provenance
item.description: A detailed record of the origin and processing history of (meta)data.
item.grounding_span: associated with detailed provenance

item.name: Domain-relevant community standards
item.description: Community-endorsed standards that (meta)data should meet for a given domain.
item.grounding_span: domain-relevant community standards

item.name: Computational agents
item.description: Autonomously acting computational data explorers that discover, access, integrate, and analyse data on behalf of humans.
item.grounding_span: computational agents

item.name: Computational stakeholders
item.description: The applications and computational agents, increasingly relevant, that undertake data retrieval and analysis.
item.grounding_span: computational stakeholders

item.name: Special-purpose repositories
item.description: Well-curated, deeply-integrated archives (e.g. GenBank, wwPDB, UniProt) for specific important digital object types.
item.grounding_span: special-purpose repositories

item.name: General-purpose data repositories
item.description: Repositories accepting a wide range of data types and formats with few descriptor requirements, contributing to a decentralized, less integrated ecosystem.
item.grounding_span: general-purpose data repositories

item.name: Data discovery
item.description: The process of finding task-appropriate scientific data and other scholarly digital objects.
item.grounding_span: data discovery

item.name: Data reuse
item.description: The reuse and integration of data by third parties after publication.
item.grounding_span: discovery and reuse

item.name: RDF
item.description: A globally-accepted framework for data and knowledge representation intended to be read and interpreted by machines.
item.grounding_span: Resource Description Framework

item.name: Linked data
item.description: Data published as interlinked, machine-readable resources enabling interoperability and reuse.
item.grounding_span: published as linked data

item.name: Knowledge discovery
item.description: The discovery and innovation that good data management is a conduit toward.
item.grounding_span: knowledge discovery and innovation

item.name: Reproducibility
item.description: The reproducibility and transparency of research enabled by making all components of the research process available.
item.grounding_span: reproducibility, and reuse

item.name: Analytical pipelines and workflows
item.description: Non-data research objects (algorithms, tools, workflows) whose formal publication is needed for transparency and reproducibility.
item.grounding_span: from data to analytical pipelines

item.name: Searchable resource
item.description: A registry or index in which (meta)data are registered or indexed to be found.
item.grounding_span: registered or indexed in a searchable resource

item.verbatim_text: JDDCP—Joint Declaration of Data Citation Principles; Acknowledging data as a first-class research output, and to support good research practices around data re-use, JDDCP proposes a set of guiding principles for citation of data within scholarly literature, another dataset, or any other research object.

item.name: Generative Engine
item.description: A search system that uses LLMs to retrieve documents and synthesize natural-language responses.

item.name: Large Language Model
item.description: The core model that retrieves and generates responses in generative engines.
item.grounding_span: large language models (LLMs)

item.name: Generative Engine Optimization
item.description: Optimizing web documents to increase their visibility in generative engine responses.
item.grounding_span: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)

item.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: Pipeline that retrieves relevant documents and synthesizes their content into responses.
item.grounding_span: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)

item.description: Classic optimization to improve web document ranking on search engines, paralleled by GEO.

item.description: Extracted rules capturing how generative engines prioritize retrieved content.

item.description: Measure of whether rewriting preserves response quality and reliability.

item.description: RL procedure used to optimize AutoGEO Mini using rule-based rewards.
